messages.subject: Unexpected Model Fit Comparison
parts:
Hello!

I am receiving unexpected model fit comparisons when I am comparing nested models. The degrees of freedom are jumping at large intervals when I am adding one interaction at a time. The AIC and BIC are also increasing in each subsequent model at astonishingly high quantities. Chisquare is also remaining significant with each subsequent model.

I am not sure why this is happening because I know each moderator is significant since I ran regressions with interaction between moderators and my latent factor and these were significant. Also, each model has good fit individually, making the anova results seem unexpected. 

I am not sure why this is happening. I would appreciate any guidance possible. I have attached the code I ran from beginning to end but had to replace variable names due to data confidentiality. The code is shown in the word document attached to this post.

Thank you for your assistance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected Model Fit Comparison
parts:
As the error message tells you, these models are not nested because they are not based on the same data.  When you add an interaction term, you are not just adding effects, you are adding variables (product terms) as input data.  To see what I mean, look at the output of:

lavInspect(DV1Fit, "sampstat")
lavInspect(DV2Fit, "sampstat")
lavInspect(DV3Fit, "sampstat")

Since this is not a software-specific issue, you might want to post your issue on SEMNET if you have more questions about not being able to compare models fit to different data.

www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen

Thank you for your reply and for this clarification. Looking at the output to the code you demonstrated, I see that lavInspect shows that each model I thought was nested utilizes a different number of variables. 

If I may ask a more specific question to lavaan, I am trying to make the models all based off the same data in order to make them nested. My understanding is that each subsequent model is nested if there is a new additional parameter included, and this parameter is what is to be compared between models. In my case, each additional moderator variable added one at a time (through the latent variable-moderator interaction), is indicative of a new parameter to compare to the previous model. 

So in order to base each model off the same dataset, is there a way lavaan can recognize that each model will use the same amount of variables, and the only difference between models will be the actual variables specified? 

Thank you again your time and assistance with this endeavor. I appreciate it!

With regards,

messages.subject: Re: Unexpected Model Fit Comparison
parts:
Shubam,
I am not sure that I am correctly reconstructing what you want to do.  Would something like this serve your purpose?

require(lavaan)

simMod <- '
  x ~~ 1*x
  m1 ~~ 1*m1
  m2 ~~ 1*m2
  x ~~ .3*m1
  x ~~ .3*m2
  m1 ~~ .3*m2'

XM <- simulateData(simMod)

xm1 <- XM$x * XM$m1
xm2 <- XM$x * XM$m2

y <- 1*XM$x + 1*XM$m1 + 1*XM$m2 + 1*xm1 + rnorm(500,0,.5)

YXM <- data.frame(XM, xm1, xm2, y)

fitMod1 <- '
  y ~ x + m1 + m2 + 0*xm1 + 0*xm2
  y ~~ y '

fitMod2 <- '
  y ~ x + m1 + m2 + xm1 + 0*xm2
  y ~~ y '

fitMod3 <- '
  y ~ x + m1 + m2 + xm1 + xm2
  y ~~ y '


fit1 <- lavaan(fitMod1, data=YXM)
fit2 <- lavaan(fitMod2, data=YXM)
fit3 <- lavaan(fitMod3, data=YXM)

lavTestLRT(fit1, fit2, fit3)

identical(lavInspect(fit1, 'sampstat'), lavInspect(fit2, 'sampstat'))
identical(lavInspect(fit1, 'sampstat'), lavInspect(fit3, 'sampstat'))

Keith
